Are you interested in making a difference in the lives of fellow Californians while achieving your career goals? Job Description And Duties
Do you have strong technical skills in research and data analysis? Are you interested in making a meaningful impact on the lives children and families across California? If so, consider joining the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB) at the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) as a Research Data Analyst (RDA) II, also considering RDA I. This position is part of a dynamic team that is dedicated to serving, aiding and protecting children and adults in ways that strengthen and preserve families, encourage personal responsibility and foster independence. We are looking for a highly motivated Research Data Analyst I/II (RDA I/II) with strong analytical skills who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment to join the Children’s Estimates Unit of the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB) team. The Children’s Estimates Unit develops the annual Local Assistance Governor’s Budget and May Revision update for Children’s programs administered by the County Welfare Departments. In addition, the FFB is responsible for providing a fiscal analysis of proposed legislative bills that have a potential impact to the Department.

The RDA II’s serve as a senior analysts that working with minimal direction, while the RDA I supports complex analysis under general direction. It is essential for the RDA I/II to possess strong analytical skills to conceptualize, develop, and create fiscal estimates that are robust and consider multiple variables (e.g., funding environment, political considerations, data integration). The work intersects with multiple branches across the department and the RDA I/II needs to develop strong working relationships to be successful. The work produced is highly visible and will be scrutinized closely by senior management, executive staff, and external stakeholders because it will have direct implications for the State Budget.

It is desirable that the RDA I/II have an understanding of social service programs’ policies and experience in interpreting and applying statutes, regulations, and following procedures. Additionally, the RDA I/II must be able to work independently, reason logically, and possess strong analytical skills. The RDA I/II is expected to mentor junior staff members, take a lead role in complex assignments, and work as an acting manager when required.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Function Summary

Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

Generic Scope

Professional who applies acquired job skills, policies, and procedures to complete substantive assignments / projects / tasks of moderate scope and complexity; exercises judgment within defined guidelines and practices to determine appropriate action.

Custom Scope

This is a part-time (50% FTE) Research Data Analyst position supporting two investigators conducting research on substance use, addiction, and harm reduction services across diverse clinical and community settings. The analyst will contribute to multiple research projects, with a primary focus on data management, statistical analysis, interpretation, and visualization.

The ideal candidate will have training or experience in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, or a related field, and mixed-methods research skills. Experience working with both large and small datasets, including data cleaning, preparation, management, sycronization, and statistical analysis, is required. Proficiency in R is strongly preferred, particularly for statistical analysis and data visualization, and experience with ArcGIS is desirable. Knowledge of or experience working with harm reduction programs, substance use treatment settings, low-barrier clinics, or populations affected by substance use is preferred. The successful candidate should be comfortable working collaboratively across multiple projects and investigators and translating analytic findings into clear tables, figures, presentations, and manuscripts.

Department Overview

The Division of Prevention Science is a leading force in prevention research innovation. We conduct transformative research, bridging communities and overcoming health inequities through high-impact prevention. The division was established within the Department of Medicine in 1991 and is the administrative home of the Center for AIDS Prevention Studies (CAPS), and the Prevention Research Center (PRC). The division is committed to advancing knowledge in prevention and has extensive expertise in social and behavioral research applied to prevention science and the development of effective prevention interventions across several disease domains. The research focus is risk behavior and reduction; epidemiology of the virus; evaluation of HIV testing procedures, demographic variables and sexual self-identification; and training for providers who care for HIV AIDS patients. While much of the work in DPS has traditionally focused on HIV/AIDS, many investigators are doing important work in other fields including cardiovascular disease, cancer, mental health, and substance abuse. The Division is composed of approximately 35 academics (faculty, fellows and specialists) and 45 non-academic staff who come from a variety of social, behavioral and policy science academic disciplines, including psychology, sociology, anthropology, epidemiology, history, political science, economics, demography, nursing, pharmacy and statistics.

The Division is home to three federally funded research centers that provide valuable infrastructure support: 1) The Center for AIDS Prevention Studies, funded by the National Institute of Mental Health; 2) The UCSF Prevention Research Center, funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3) three evaluation centers funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and 4) a newly-funded research coordinating center to reduce disparities in multiple chronic diseases, funded by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities. The Division is also home to the Center of Excellence for Transgender Health and over 100 active sponsored research projects.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Experience conducting epidemiological studies using large and small datasets, and working knowledge of research function.
Working skills in statistical analysis, systems programming, database design and data security measures.
Experience in data management and analysis using R and geospatial analysis using ArcGIS software programs.
Communicates complex information in a clear and concise manner both verbally and in writing.
At least one year of experience working with harm reduction organizations, treatment center or low barrier clinics that serve people with a substance use disorder.

Preferred Qualifications

Working skills in conducting interviews and administering surveys (data collection).
Experience working on mixed methods studies that integrates qualitative and quantitative datasets.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Preferred Education

Master’s degree in biostatistics, epidemiology or another closely related field.

Licenses

None listed.

About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

The Graduate Funding Unit plays a central role in maintaining the highest level of academic excellence possible at UC Berkeley. We provide fellowships, funding, and program support to attract the most competitive students to our university and provide funding opportunities for students at various stages of their academic career. Our programs exist to give students opportunities to devote themselves fully to the pursuit of their scholarly and professional interests. Our knowledge and expertise in all areas of graduate funding and student life provide a strong foundation for advising the students, faculty, and staff across our vast and diverse campus.

The Student Funding team trains and advises staff and faculty departmental advisors in over 125 degree programs, offers direct advising to approximately 13,000 graduate and professional students, as well as individuals seeking admission into a graduate program at Berkeley. Training and expertise includes fellowship and academic support funding and collective bargaining agreement administration for academic student employees and graduate student researchers.

Position Summary

The Fellowships Program Coordinator plays a significant role in supporting graduate students through the administration of Graduate Division, Campus, National, and International fellowship programs on behalf of the campus. This position works with internal and external organizations to coordinate graduate student fellowships, providing support to students, faculty, and staff from application to evaluation to awarding. The Fellowships Program Coordinator serves as an expert resource to update formulas and eligibility requirements according to national and constituent regulations and policies, ensuring proper payment of awards and monitoring compliance with fellowship terms. Additionally, this position administers and tracks the current University Fellowship allocation system, analyzes data to ensure compliance and accurate aid delivery, and partners with departmental staff to provide accurate and transparent information about funding to help students achieve their academic goals.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst for Lab Production Support, Extended-Hours Support (ExHS)
jobs.description:
Important: this position will work on the Weekend Shift team, with the following rotation schedules:

Tuesday-to-Saturday (including Tue, Wed, Thur, Fri, and Sat), 9AM-to-5PM.
Sunday-to-Thursday (including Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, and Thur), 9AM-to-5PM.

This position will rotate through the above work schedules quarterly, i.e., work in one rotation schedule for 3 calendar months, and then move to the other rotation schedule for another 3 calendar months.

This is an exciting opportunity in our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department at Natera (a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing), to provide critical data analytics support for our lab production operations. As a Senior Data Analyst for Lab Production Support in our DSPE Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) team, you will work in the Weekend Shift team (following the above two rotation schedules). You will have the opportunity to apply innovative data analytics solutions, directly support the most cutting-edge medical diagnostics and genomics applications, and make real & immediate impact to patients and healthcare providers, by providing timely & accurate data analysis support to Natera's production laboratories, as well as for other key business needs.

Primary Responsibilities

Technical Execution and Infrastructure

Deliver timely data support to Lab Operations teams, unblock production issues, and improve patient results turnaround times.
Apply statistical techniques to analyze complex datasets, diagnose operational issues, and support data-driven decision-making.
Perform exploratory data analysis, identify trends, and work with stakeholders to interpret findings and drive continuous improvement.
Design and implement automated solutions for recurring data analysis and production support workflows, improving operational efficiency and scalability.
Extract, transform, and analyze data to generate actionable insights that support lab production operations and business decisions.
Document analytical processes, best practices, and insights to ensure consistency and knowledge transfer across teams.

Process Improvement

Develop and optimize solutions for efficient data retrieval and scalable performance on large and/or complex datasets.
Learn and acquire operational efficiencies on new technologies and solutions developed by other DSPE teams.
Train and coach junior team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Lab Operations and Product teams to identify process issues, assist with root cause analysis, and provide product support.
Represent the Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) team in stakeholder meetings.
Effectively and correctly escalate encountered issues to other DSPE teams.

Qualifications

Masters degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Operational Research, or other related fields.
Minimum 3 years of relevant industry experience.
Minimum 3 years of experience working in a highly regulated environment (e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings).
Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in data analysis, extraction, querying in production support roles.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Working knowledge of the business processes and requirements of diagnostic laboratories. Knowledge of molecular biology, genetics, genomics, and/or bioinformatics is a plus.
Proficient in data analysis and statistical techniques.
Proficient in Python and SQL development.
Working knowledge of Snowflake platform and cloud technologies.
Strong understanding of statistical concepts such as hypothesis testing, central limit theorem, time series analysis, anomaly detection, and regression modeling.
Good documentation practices and coding style.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience using version control systems such as GitHub or GitLab for managing code and collaboration.
Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment.
Strong interpersonal skills.
Strong integrity.

Compensation & Total Rewards

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

Annual performance incentive bonus
Long-term equity awards
Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
401(k) with company match
Generous paid time off and company holidays
Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range

$145,000—$170,000 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

What We Offer

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

For more information, visit www.natera.com.

We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide.

jobs.description:
Type of Appointment:
Full Time, Probationary

Job Classification:
Student Services Professional III

Anticipated Hiring Range:
$5,540 per month

Work Schedule:
Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; schedule may vary based on operational needs and may include occasional evenings and weekends in support of orientation and transition programs.

The Department

New Student Programs and Family Engagement is responsible for preparing entering students for academic and personal success by providing an effective transition to the university from the point of admission through the end of the students' first year. New Student Programs and Family Engagement provides information, communications, and services to incoming students and their support system to orient them to the traditions, mission, philosophy, and culture of the campus and to make them knowledgeable about Cal Poly Pomona's opportunities, resources, challenges, and programs. New Student Programs and Family Engagement designs, plans, implements, and assesses mandatory online and in-person orientation events, as well as the ongoing engagement of family members and supporters throughout the academic year. The position will bring together existing decentralized institutional programs, services and activities for parents and families under one functional administrative structure to ensure optimum coordination and resource management, timely response and referral and identification of additional opportunities to enhance parent/family relations and outreach. New Student Programs and Family Engagement serves as the administrative office for the mandatory student orientation programs, parent/family orientation, and parent/family communication. The office is responsible for compliance with federal, state, CSU System, and University requirements and the timely and accurate dissemination of information to students, parents, families, supporters, and campus constituents. New Student Programs and Family Engagement is housed within the Division of Student Affairs and is part of the Student Experience cluster that reports to the Director of New Student Programs and Family Engagement. New Student Programs and Family Engagement works collaboratively with campus partners in support of enrollment management goals, student success and retention, equity and belonging, and institutional planning efforts. The Division of Student Affairs strives for excellence through a shared student-centered philosophy and values of collaboration, inclusivity, integrity, innovation, and student-centeredness. In performing the duties assigned to this position, the incumbent is expected to consistently demonstrate attitudes and behaviors that are in keeping with the division's philosophy and values.

Duties And Responsibilities

Student Leader Development & Program Leadership

Coordinate the recruitment, selection, onboarding, and training of approximately 40 Orientation Captains and Orientation Leaders.
Recommend student employees for hire and, when necessary, recommend appropriate corrective action or separation in consultation with the Senior Coordinator and Director.
Develop and implement training that prepares student leaders to support incoming students and families during orientation and transition programs.
Develop student staff work schedules and assign duties based on orientation and program needs.
Provide day-to-day work direction, coaching, feedback, and clarification of performance and conduct expectations.
Monitor student staff performance and provide input into performance evaluations in accordance with department and university practices. Develop learning opportunities for student leaders in areas such as communication, conflict resolution, peer support, student wellbeing, customer service, campus resources, and referral practices.
Evaluate the effectiveness of student-leader training and recommend improvements based on program needs and assessment results.

Orientation and Transition Planning & Implementation

Plan and coordinate orientation and transition programs in collaboration with the Senior Coordinator, Director, and campus partners.
Develop program learning outcomes, activities, and assessment strategies that support incoming students' transition to the university.
Coordinate New Student Convocation, welcome activities, and other transition experiences, including program logistics, campus partnerships, communications, and implementation.
Analyze participant feedback, program assessment results, and identified student needs to recommend improvements to orientation and transition programming.
Research and recommend student engagement activities that support peer connection, belonging, student success, and continued transition throughout the first year.
Serve as a program lead during assigned orientation and transition programs, coordinating student staff and addressing operational or student-service issues within established guidelines.
Collaborate with Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, colleges, and other university departments to coordinate information, resources, and services for incoming students.

New Student Enrollment Support

Provide information and guidance to incoming students regarding orientation, transition, and enrollment-related processes.
Identify the nature of student concerns, explain applicable university processes and requirements, and assist students in identifying appropriate resources and available courses of action.
Refer students to academic advising, enrollment services, student support programs, or other campus resources as appropriate.
Collaborate with Academic Affairs, college advising units, and other campus partners to address recurring orientation and transition-related student issues.

Administrative Support

Perform administrative tasks related to orientation leader supervision and orientation program planning, including room reservations, procurement card reconciliation, IT Security/ATI review requests, purchase order requisitions, and budget ledger entries.

Student Affairs/University Committees

Represent New Student Programs and Family Engagement on a variety of divisional and campus-wide committees.

Graduate Intern Management

In partnership with other professional staff, recruit, interview, recommend for hire, train, and provide work direction to seasonal graduate student interns.
Provide task direction, work assignments, performance feedback, and clarification of conduct expectations; recommend appropriate corrective action in consultation with professional staff as needed.
Ensure graduate interns execute their responsibilities appropriately and effectively as representatives of the department, division, and university.
Ensure graduate interns follow university employment guidelines and comply with labor law.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree - Equivalent to graduation from a four-year college or university in a related field, including or supplemented by upper division or graduate coursework in counseling techniques, interviewing, and conflict resolution where such are job-related.
Possession of these knowledge and abilities is typically demonstrated through the equivalent of three years of progressively responsible professional student services work experience. One year in the program area to which assigned may be preferred but is not required.
A master’s degree in Counseling, Clinical Psychology, Social Work, or a directly related field may be substituted for one year of experience. A doctorate degree and the appropriate internship or clinical training in counseling or guidance may be substituted for the three years of experience for positions with a major responsibility for professional career or personal counseling.
Driver's license, Valid and in State
Thorough knowledge of the principles of individual and group behavior.
General knowledge of the principles, practices and trends of the Student Services field as well as general knowledge of the policies, procedures and practices of the program area to which assigned; general knowledge of individual counseling techniques; general knowledge, or the ability to rapidly acquire such knowledge, of the organizational procedures and activities of the specific campus to which the position is assigned. Working knowledge of student services programs outside the program to which immediately assigned.
Ability to analyze complex situations accurately and adopt effective courses of action; advise students individually and in groups on complex student‑related matters; determine appropriate courses of action and proper techniques to utilize while engaged with individuals in personal interactions of an argumentative or sensitive nature; interpret and evaluate descriptions and explanations of problems brought forward by individuals or student organizations, analyze and define the problem, draw valid conclusions and project consequences of various alternative courses of action; carry out a variety of professionally complex assignments without detailed instructions; and establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with a variety of individuals.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in higher education, student affairs, counseling, education, or a related field.
Experience coordinating orientation, transition, student success, or related Student Services programs.
Experience training and providing work direction to student employees or peer leaders.
Experience with program planning, event coordination, assessment, and evaluation. Knowledge of student development and learning theory as related to student transition and student success.

Strong written, oral, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

jobs.title: Senior Hydrogeologist
jobs.description:
As a Senior Hydrogeologist, you will play a key role in managing a variety of complex and rewarding projects, including groundwater supply investigations, groundwater control assessments, aquifer testing and analysis, stormwater infiltration assessments, groundwater flow modeling, and hydrogeologic/hydrologic analysis. Responsibilities include planning and overseeing hydrogeologic field investigations, leading technical discussions with field staff, and managing project tasks such as budgeting, scheduling, and client communications. You will conduct and supervise hydrogeologic analyses and groundwater modeling, prepare technical reports, and perform site visits to support data collection and field oversight. As a senior team member, you will also be responsible for mentoring junior staff and providing technical leadership across project teams and lead business-development activities such as identifying potential new clients, attending conferences or professional association meetings, and assisting with proposal development.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Leads all project management tasks such as developing budgets and scopes, client billings, field report reviews, contract reviews, and proposal development. Partners with Principals and Associates to ensure effective execution of multiple projects.
Serves as a technical resource for clients and project staff; provides guidance and expertise to solve complex challenges.
Develops complete and accurate field reports, figures, tables, etc., that require minimal edits or revisions.
Reviews deliverables from staff and mid-level employees such as field reports, calculations, analyses, etc. Mentors junior staff relative to technical skills, consulting best practices, etc.
Leads business-development activities such as identifying potential new clients, attending conferences or professional association meetings, etc.

Job Function Summary

Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

Generic Scope

Professional who applies acquired job skills, policies, and procedures to complete substantive assignments / projects / tasks of moderate scope and complexity; exercises judgment within defined guidelines and practices to determine appropriate action.

Custom Scope

This is a part-time (50% FTE) Research Data Analyst position supporting two investigators conducting research on substance use, addiction, and harm reduction services across diverse clinical and community settings. The analyst will contribute to multiple research projects, with a primary focus on data management, statistical analysis, interpretation, and visualization.

The ideal candidate will have training or experience in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, or a related field, and mixed-methods research skills. Experience working with both large and small datasets, including data cleaning, preparation, management, sycronization, and statistical analysis, is required. Proficiency in R is strongly preferred, particularly for statistical analysis and data visualization, and experience with ArcGIS is desirable. Knowledge of or experience working with harm reduction programs, substance use treatment settings, low-barrier clinics, or populations affected by substance use is preferred. The successful candidate should be comfortable working collaboratively across multiple projects and investigators and translating analytic findings into clear tables, figures, presentations, and manuscripts.

Department Overview

The Division of Prevention Science is a leading force in prevention research innovation. We conduct transformative research, bridging communities and overcoming health inequities through high-impact prevention. The division was established within the Department of Medicine in 1991 and is the administrative home of the Center for AIDS Prevention Studies (CAPS), and the Prevention Research Center (PRC). The division is committed to advancing knowledge in prevention and has extensive expertise in social and behavioral research applied to prevention science and the development of effective prevention interventions across several disease domains. The research focus is risk behavior and reduction; epidemiology of the virus; evaluation of HIV testing procedures, demographic variables and sexual self-identification; and training for providers who care for HIV AIDS patients. While much of the work in DPS has traditionally focused on HIV/AIDS, many investigators are doing important work in other fields including cardiovascular disease, cancer, mental health, and substance abuse. The Division is composed of approximately 35 academics (faculty, fellows and specialists) and 45 non-academic staff who come from a variety of social, behavioral and policy science academic disciplines, including psychology, sociology, anthropology, epidemiology, history, political science, economics, demography, nursing, pharmacy and statistics.

The Division is home to three federally funded research centers that provide valuable infrastructure support: 1) The Center for AIDS Prevention Studies, funded by the National Institute of Mental Health; 2) The UCSF Prevention Research Center, funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3) three evaluation centers funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and 4) a newly-funded research coordinating center to reduce disparities in multiple chronic diseases, funded by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities. The Division is also home to the Center of Excellence for Transgender Health and over 100 active sponsored research projects.

Required Qualifications

Experience conducting epidemiological studies using large and small datasets, and working knowledge of research function.
Working skills in statistical analysis, systems programming, database design and data security measures.
Experience in data management and analysis using R and geospatial analysis using ArcGIS software programs.
Communicates complex information in a clear and concise manner both verbally and in writing.
At least one year of experience working with harm reduction organizations, treatment center or low barrier clinics that serve people with a substance use disorder.

Preferred Qualifications

Working skills in conducting interviews and administering surveys (data collection).
Experience working on mixed methods studies that integrates qualitative and quantitative datasets.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Preferred Education

Master’s degree in biostatistics, epidemiology or another closely related field.

Exercises professional judgment to authorize changes in financial aid awards.

Coordinates follow up inquiries when allocations are underused by departments.

Streamlines Slate workflows, create and manage new data fields, and manage departmental applications.
Assist with Funding Offer Letter Template development, implementation, maintenance, and training.
Assist departments with entering admitted student funding packages.

Research and recommend student engagement activities that support peer connection, belonging, student success, and continued transition throughout the first year.

Collaborate with Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, colleges, and other university departments to coordinate information, resources, and services for incoming students.

Collaborate with Academic Affairs, college advising units, and other campus partners to address recurring orientation and transition-related student issues.

Possession of these knowledge and abilities is typically demonstrated through the equivalent of three years of progressively responsible professional student services work experience. One year in the program area to which assigned may be preferred but is not required.

Professional-level verbal and written communication skills.

Established in 2023 as UT Austin’s newest college, the School of Civic Leadership is a community of scholars and students dedicated to studying the foundational ideas and institutions of a free society, with the goal of advancing human flourishing. We value independent thought, civil discourse, reasoned deliberation, and intellectual curiosity as we prepare to meet the challenges of the present and sustain the blessings of liberty for future generations.

Join Cleveland Clinic Main Campus and experience world class healthcare at its best. Here, you will be part of a talented, compassionate, and driven team of caregivers, work with state-of-the-art technology and provide stellar patient care.

As a Perioperative Educational Program Coordinator, you will work in conjunction with the Professional Development Manager to plan, implement and evaluate departmental orientation and education activities for clinical and support caregivers. This position is a great way to share your knowledge and skills with other caregivers while creating opportunities for others to learn and grow. There are multiple options for professional development in this role, such as certifications, advanced education, distinguished educator certificate and simulation fellowships.

A caregiver in this position works days from 7:00AM – 4:00PM.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

Plan and implement orientation for new hires.
Assist education caregivers in assigning unit preceptors.
Assist in interviewing new caregivers.
Complete probationary performance evaluations for new hires and participate in annual evaluations with unit managers.
Coordinate continuing education and training programs and staff development within the department.
Assist in coordinating programs with local colleges and universities.
Perform patient care up to 20% of work time in area of clinical expertise in order to demonstrate clinical competence and be able to teach others.
Actively assist the management team with ensuring caregiver compliance with regulatory requirements. This may include training and recertification for CPR, ACLS, annual education on fire safety, diversity, code management, HIPPAA and coordination of TB testing.

Minimum qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)
Current state licensure as a Registered Nurse (RN)
Basic Life Support (BLS) certification through the American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross
If performing moderate/procedural sedation, must have Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) certification through the American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross within six months of hire
Two years of perioperative experience, specifically in circulating/OR setting
Demonstrated expertise in a clinical specialty with current patient care competence
Knowledge of adult learning theory, motivational strategies, change theory, group process skills, leadership strategies and teaching
Demonstrated computer skills utilizing clinical systems (Epic/Optime) and Microsoft applications (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)

Preferred qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

Master’s Degree

Physical Requirements:

Requires corrected vision and hearing to normal range.
Requires working under stressful conditions of working irregular hours.
Requires some exposure to communicable diseases or bodily fluids.

Follows standard precautions using personal protective equipment as required.
